obligations.summary: The Commission may adopt implementing acts establishing common specifications for high-risk AI system requirements or GPAI model obligations when standardisation conditions (failed or insufficient harmonised standards) are fulfilled, after consulting the advisory forum and following the examination procedure.
exceptions: Common specifications are only adopted if: (a) a request to a European standardisation organisation was not accepted, or the harmonised standard was not delivered on time, or it insufficiently addresses fundamental rights concerns, or it does not comply with the request; and (b) no reference to relevant harmonised standards has been or is expected to be published in the Official Journal.

obligations.summary: Before preparing a draft implementing act on common specifications, the Commission must inform the committee referred to in Article 22 of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 that the conditions in paragraph 1 are fulfilled.

High-risk AI systems or general-purpose AI models that conform to adopted common specifications shall be presumed to be in conformity with the corresponding requirements or obligations to the extent those specifications cover them.
exceptions: Presumption of conformity applies only to the extent the common specifications actually cover the relevant requirements or obligations.

obligations.summary: When a reference to a harmonised standard covering the same requirements is published in the Official Journal, the Commission must repeal the relevant implementing acts or the parts thereof that cover the same requirements.

Providers of high-risk AI systems or general-purpose AI models that do not comply with adopted common specifications must duly justify that their alternative technical solutions meet the relevant requirements or obligations to at least an equivalent level.
exceptions: Non-compliance with common specifications is permitted if the provider can justify that their technical solutions achieve at least equivalent compliance with the underlying requirements or obligations.

obligations.summary: Where a Member State considers that a common specification does not entirely meet the applicable requirements or obligations, it must inform the Commission with a detailed explanation, and the Commission must assess that information and, if appropriate, amend the implementing act.
